data.body: de95 FLAKE ROOT-CAUSED (the /rebar-debug agent DISPROVED the ticket's own stated cause). Ticket claimed os.path.isdir(_config.tracker_dir()) in mcp_server.main() was False under a cwd/tracker-dir leak; a runtime probe under the exact failing order showed tracker_dir() resolving correctly with isdir=True. No production bug exists. Real mechanism: tests/unit/test_ensures_late_binding.py pops rebar._store.ensures from sys.modules, re-imports it, and restores ONLY sys.modules - but loading a submodule also setattrs it on the parent package, so two copies stay live. 'from rebar._store import ensures' resolves via getattr(package,...) (IMPORT_FROM falls back to sys.modules only on AttributeError), so test_fsck_ensures.py monkeypatches the ORIGINAL while mcp_server.main()'s function-local import at mcp_server.py:714 gets the FRESH UNPATCHED one - the real run_ensures ran and order came back ['run']. Order-dependence comes from pytest-xdist; the repo has no pytest-randomly dependency at all, so that part of the ticket was also wrong. Origin: commit 1496adf2b2 (ticket d720-fc72-3763-4cac) - itself an ordering-pollution fix that introduced a new bug of the SAME class. Fix is a _reimportable() context manager restoring both bindings in a finally; 3 test files, no production file touched, no assertion weakened, no retry/xfail/sleep. Mutation-checked: deleting the restoring line returns both the new oracle and the original symptom to RED. Pushed as Gerrit 2072; a landing agent owns submit + close with --caused-by=d720-fc72-3763-4cac --class=regression. This matters to the epic because this flake is what produced the spurious Verified -1 on changes 2047 and 2057.
